# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60 (Bu-Vb Pc60)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc60
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60
**Title (English, from literature):** Hiding a robe

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Cīvaraapanidhāna* ("Hiding a robe"), cataloged as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60, lays down an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for a monk who hides or causes to be hidden the requisites of another monastic—including their robe, bowl, or sitting mat (*nisīdana*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In her analysis of Vinaya regulations, Ute Hüsken notes that this rule against hiding requisites provides key textual evidence that monastics possessed items such as sitting mats, and points out that the word-by-word commentary (*padabhājaniya*) to this rule preserves standard definitions and measurements of requisites, such as the three permissible bowl capacities (large, medium, and small) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its origin story has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this prohibition was shared across all major early Buddhist Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. It corresponds to Pācittiya 60 of the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra, and to Pācittiya 141 in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other lineages are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan versions of the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka traditions [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects extensive internal formulaic overlap within the Pali Vinaya, showing substantial shared passages with other Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules including Pācittiya 55, 74, 77, and Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) and Prātimokṣa commentaries [DharmaNexus], agreeing with SuttaCentral's curated Mūlasarvāstivāda parallels [SuttaCentral].
